why: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) The quoted sentence exists VERBATIM in curl'd https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp.md, line 891, under '### Tool output exceeds maximum allowed tokens'. The whole line is three sentences and the other two reinforce rather than reverse it: 'The SDK applies the same MCP output limit as Claude Code.' before it, and 'Raise the limit with the MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment variable.' after it, plus a pointer to /docs/en/mcp#mcp-output-limits-and-warnings 'including how a server can declare a higher per-tool limit'. Cross-checked against code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md: ':1022 Default limit: the default maximum is 25,000 tokens', ':1021 Configurable limit ... MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS', ':1040 up to a hard ceiling of 500,000 characters'. (2) The cited lines say exactly what was claimed: packages/shared/src/utils/large-response.ts:42 'export const TOKEN_LIMIT = 12000' and :57 'export const MAX_DECLARED_RESULT_SIZE_CHARS = 500_000'. (3) Layer up and layer down both hold, and the subsystem is the right one. Layer down: MCP tool results reach the guard at packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:2171 (guardLargeResult inside callTool), which passes maxResultSizeChars from declaredResultSizeChars() reading _meta['anthropic/maxResultSizeChars'] (MCP_MAX_RESULT_SIZE_CHARS_META_KEY, mcp-pool.ts:213; clamp at large-response.ts:620-628) but passes NO contextWindow, so the effective persist threshold on the MCP path is the flat TOKEN_LIMIT of 12000 via tokenLimitFor(undefined) (large-response.ts:141-147, 633). The persist-to-disk shape itself matches the doc (saveLargeResponse -> long_responses/, formatLargeResponseMessage names the absolute path), so the divergence is the NUMBER and the missing override, not the mechanism. Layer up: the other production guard site, claude-agent.ts:1829, passes contextWindow, which can only LOWER the threshold (min(TOKEN_LIMIT, 10% of window), floor 2000) - nothing anywhere raises it to 25000. Absence verified binary-safe with grep -ran across the repo excluding node_modules/.references/dist: MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS appears ONLY in docs (parity audit :1787, r-queue-doc-verification :342, the two doc-sweep JSONs) and in zero source files; no NESSY_-prefixed counterpart exists either, and large-response.ts contains no process.env read at all. This is not a rename artifact: the same file's sibling knob IS ported under the fork prefix (mcp-pool.ts:1959 reads NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT for CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT), so the pattern exists and this one env var simply has no counterpart. Not an owner decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions - none touch MCP output limits. Not a deliberate product difference either (no subscription-flow, gateway or rename involvement). The 12000 value does carry a reason in its own doc comment (lowered from 15k after a base64-heavy result poisoned a session), and 2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:342 flags the area as needing a decision, but neither is a recorded ruling that the user-facing override may be absent.
correctedState: Confirmed as claimed, with the mechanism working and only the number and the override missing. MCP tool results are persisted to disk and replaced with a file-referencing message (mcp-pool.ts:2171 -> guardLargeResult -> handleLargeResponse -> long_responses/), but the threshold is the flat TOKEN_LIMIT = 12000 estimated tokens (large-response.ts:42; the MCP call site passes no contextWindow, and contextWindow can only lower it) rather than the documented 25,000, and no MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS or NESSY_-prefixed override is read anywhere in the repo - verified with grep -ran, which finds the name only in docs. The per-tool half IS implemented and clamped to the documented 500,000-character ceiling (MAX_DECLARED_RESULT_SIZE_CHARS at :57, read from _meta['anthropic/maxResultSizeChars'] at mcp-pool.ts:213/1933). One nuance beyond the claim: our declared allowance only RAISES the threshold (large-response.ts:617-628), whereas mcp.md:1023/1054 says a declaring tool uses that value 'instead ... regardless of what MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS is set to', so a server declaring a value BELOW our 12k-equivalent is not honoured downward.
